//: Part 19 §19.9.2 — the bundle budgets, as a committed file so that raising one
is a reviewable line in a diff rather than an argument in a PR thread.
Enforced by `npm run bundle:check` (scripts/check-bundle.mjs), which reads the
real `next build` output: `.next/build-manifest.json` for the framework chunks
and every `.next/server/app/**/page_client-reference-manifest.js` for the
per-route entry chunks. Every number here is KILOBYTES OF GZIP (level 9) — the
thing the merchant's phone downloads — not raw bytes.
Definitions, so a number here means one thing only:
framework  build-manifest `rootMainFiles` minus `polyfillFiles`: react-dom,
the Next client runtime, the Turbopack loader.
sharedApp  the chunks EVERY app route loads, minus framework. Redux, axios,
react-intl + en.json, and whatever else has leaked into the shell.
route      a route's first-load set minus framework and sharedApp.
firstLoad  framework + sharedApp + route. What a cold visit costs.
The legacy polyfill chunk is excluded everywhere: Next emits it with
`noModule`, so a modern browser never downloads it. Counting it would add ~38 KB
to every figure and make the budgets meaningless.
`routes` keys are the URL path, route groups stripped: the manifest's
`/(app)/parties/page` is matched by `/parties`. Anything unnamed falls to
`default`.
Three route budgets were raised here, and the reason is measured, not
estimated. `UbSelect` was a native <select> standing in for a combobox the
unreachable ml-uikit could not supply; vendoring the real package makes it a
Radix composite, which costs ~20-28 KB gz on a route that renders one.
What that buys: a positioned menu that cannot exceed its trigger's width, a
capped height so 38 GST states scroll instead of running off a short screen,
real keyboard navigation and type-ahead, and a chevron the design chose rather
than the platform's own — the defect the first review reported.
What it did NOT buy, deliberately: the language and theme pickers in the auth
footer stayed native. The gate caught them putting 19.5 KB on
/forgot-password and /set-password, routes with no form field at all, to
restyle a two-item list. `UbNativeSelect` exists for that case and the
baseline is unchanged at 223.5 KB.

── 21 Sep 2026: the store-shape question, ANSWERED without changing the ────
sharedApp 101.1 -> 94.8 (-6.3), so the budget comes DOWN 102 -> 96. First
reduction in this file.
The two notes above framed this as a choice between §19.3.9 standing and the
shell growing for ever, or lazily registered reducers. Both were measured
before choosing, and both framings were wrong.
Lazy reducers buy about 2 KB per slice, ~16 KB across the eight features still
to come. The price is that `RootState` is total over the store: removing one
slice to measure the ceiling produced 16 type errors across the slice, its
selectors and the invalidation map, which is the cost written down. Every
selector for a lazily registered slice would have to survive its own state
being absent, on every render before injection. That is ~15 selectors x 8
slices of defensive code to save 16 KB.
Meanwhile the single largest non-framework item in the shell was
decimal.js-light at 11 KB, and the note at the top of this file already said
why it was there: `partyListSlice` summed the page in its REDUCER, which
reaches `view-model/partyDisplay` -> `utils/money` -> decimal. So a money
library shipped to /legal/terms, /login and every other route that will never
show a rupee.
Two changes, no architecture touched: the totals TYPE and its zero value moved
out of the view-model into `constants/partyListDefaults` (a type and a
two-field object carry nothing), and the page sum moved out of the reducer
into `usePartyList`, which is route-local. -6.3 KB on every route in the
product, against -2 KB per slice for the architectural change.
The 11 KB did not vanish — it moved to the routes that do arithmetic:
/parties 79 -> 86 and /design-system 74 -> 80 on the route chunk. Both
routes' FIRST LOAD still fell, because they were paying the shell cost
anyway. That is the trade the whole file is about: the page that shows money
pays for the money library, and the page that shows a paragraph does not.
**So §19.3.9 stands.** Static registration is not what makes the shell grow;
what a slice IMPORTS is. The rule to apply before the ledger slice lands is
the one this file has stated from the beginning — ANYTHING A SLICE IMPORTS IS
ON EVERY ROUTE — and the lesson is that it applies to a reducer's
computation, not only to its dependencies. Ledger, inventory and sales all
want money arithmetic. None of it belongs in a reducer.
Also measured and rejected: lazily importing a feature's SERVICE from inside
its thunk. Worth 0.4 KB on the member slice, and it delayed the party list's
warm-up behind a chunk download — a prefetch that has to fetch its own code
first is not a prefetch. Three tests caught that, which is the warm-up's
tests doing their job.

── 22 Sep 2026: the drawn controls, and a barrel that cost 11.5 KB ────────
`MLCheckbox` and `MLRadioGroup` were native `<input>`s, which cannot be
styled — the browser draws the tick, the dot, the corner radius and the
checked fill, so they looked like Chrome on Chrome and like Safari on Safari,
beside a kit that looks like itself everywhere. Both are Radix now, matching
BrandHub, and `indeterminate` is a real state rather than a DOM property poked
through a ref.
The first measurement of that change was +11.5 KB on EVERY route, including
/forgot-password — one email field, on a route that has never had a checkbox.
Cause: both controls lived in `mlFormPrimitives.tsx` beside `MLInput`, so any
file importing a text field pulled `@radix-ui/react-checkbox` and
`@radix-ui/react-radio-group` with it. Module-level imports tree-shake BETWEEN
modules, not within one. Splitting them into their own files put
/forgot-password back to 44.0 from 55.2 and took /parties and /settings/team
back inside their budgets without changing a line of their code.
What is left is honest — these two routes really do render these components:
/onboarding/step/[n]  route  90 ->  98  (measured 96.0) — the GST-type radio
/design-system        route  80 ->  94  (measured 92.1) — the gallery renders
every control, and now also the
tooltip, popover and switch, which
are three more Radix packages

── 22 Sep 2026: the table's own states, and the column menu ───────────────
Two route budgets move, and only two, because only two routes render a grid.
**+1.2 KB on every grid route: `UbDataGridStateTable`.** The loading, empty,
filtered-empty and error states used to be drawn INSTEAD of the table — a
stack of divs, then a panel. They are now `<td>`s and one `<td colSpan>`
inside a real table with the real header, which is what BrandHub does. The
bytes buy the thing the skeleton existed for and was not delivering: with no
table under it, the skeleton had no column geometry, so `table-fixed`
redistributed every column width at the exact moment the rows landed and the
reader started reading. It is eager rather than lazy on purpose — a skeleton
that waits for a chunk is not a skeleton — and `tableChrome.ts` plus a guard
in `designSystemGuards.test.ts` keep the two tables' geometry identical.
